title: Load a delivery van in reverse route order
instruction: Load the parcels into the van so they can be unloaded in route order: the parcel for the last stop on the route card goes in deepest and the one for the first stop goes nearest the door.
context: Last-mile delivery loading: parcels go into the van in reverse stop order (last in, first out), so the driver can unload each stop without digging past other parcels. The route card gives stop order; the loader must reverse it.
setup: A wooden table; all positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, measured forward and toward the left arm. A gray open-top cargo bay (inner 170 mm deep x 75 mm wide, 6 mm walls 20 mm high, no wall on the door side facing the arms) has its inner floor from 270 to 440 mm forward, centered 130 mm toward the left arm. A white route card (90 x 30 mm) lies 400 mm forward, 30 mm toward the right arm, with three 14 mm squares listing stops 1, 2, 3 from far to near: red, green, blue. Three 45 mm cube parcels (80 g) stand 200 mm forward: green 170 mm, blue 100 mm and red 30 mm toward the left arm.
scoring: 0.2 per parcel standing upright on the bay floor with its center inside the bay. Plus 0.4 once all three are in and ordered along the bay from the back wall to the door as blue (stop 3), green (stop 2), red (stop 1), each center at least 20 mm deeper than the next. 1.0 at most. Success once all three are in, in order, and still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lift the parcels out and return them to their start positions (tape marks); the bay and card are taped down.
fidelity: Rigid boxes for the parcels, bay walls and card; the bay is fixed to the table and has no roof. Upright means the parcel's center is within 4 mm of its resting height on the bay floor. The route card's colored squares stand in for printed stop labels.
